(a) The shape of a case of the case list: built as {property, paths: the files it touches, identifiers: every identity tied to it, replace: {path: bytes}, the planted content}; a touched path must be a file the snapshot holds (a case that adds or removes a file is refused). 13a/13d may fix another shape with the harness; make follows it then. (b) The placeholder and what 'every file' means for a path: identifiers are replaced by the bytes REDACTED in every file's content; an identifier in a file's path or a link's target refuses the snapshot (identifier_in_path) rather than renaming a file, and a replacement that itself makes an identifier refuses it (sanitize_incomplete). The placeholder is visible in a planted snapshot's files and absent from a clean one's, so a reader of the files can tell them apart wherever an identity was replaced; 13c's 'which one is clean is not told' is kept for the document only (it has no kind and no case). (c) The form of snapshot_id and the manifest: {schema, snapshot_id, files: {path: sha256}, links: {path: target}, exec: [path]}, the id a sha256 over files, links and exec as sorted JSON; links are kept as written. (d) What the adapter of asama-1/05 step 2 runs on: the kos job writes the clean snapshot out and the organs get that directory as their tree, not the unit's staged worktree; 13c excludes the installed directories, so the snapshot has no node_modules, and no page says how an adapter that wraps the unit's lint tool gets that tool (the unit's env_image is the organ's image, reports/seed-073 (d)). Not built: 13c's 'profile finding_id_patterns: cleaned in comment and document lines only, string literals untouched'. The grep shows no producer of finding_id_patterns on the loop's path (profile.derive has no such field; profile.propose is a later row), and 'comment line' is not defined per language: leaving string literals untouched needs each language's lexing (a // inside a string, a # in YAML against a # in a Python string, block comments, Markdown as a whole), and a rule that guesses would either leak an id or change a literal. What is asked: the case shape, the placeholder, whether a path holding an identity renames or refuses, the definition of a comment or document line (per language, or a fixed list of line prefixes and file suffixes), who writes finding_id_patterns, and how an adapter reaches its tool on a snapshot without installed directories.
